notes: Fixes the root cause consistently: new unquoted-brace helpers on Token and Dispenser replace raw `Val()=="{"`/`"}"` checks across the dispenser, addresses, directives, doImport, directive and blockTokens, so quoted, backtick and heredoc braces become ordinary values; tests are thorough (dispenser, parse success and error cases, and an adapt integration test for the exact issue).

Fixes the root cause by adding unexported Token and Dispenser helpers that recognize only unquoted braces, and uses them consistently across the parser (directive, blockTokens, addresses, doImport snippet detection, open/close checks) and the dispenser (NextArg, NextBlock, ArgErr), backed by thorough dispenser, parser and integration adapt tests.

Adds a `Dir` field to the target path descriptor and fills it by walking the current section and its ancestors, replacing each matching path segment with that section's slug; this fixes the issue's example plus nested sections, non-section subdirectories, taxonomies and terms. The new test covers each of these cases, but the segment-index mapping via counting slashes is a bit implicit and permalink `:sections` tokens still ignore section slugs.

Adds a precomputed `Dir` to `TargetPathDescriptor` by replacing directory segments with ancestor section, taxonomy and term slugs; this handles nested sections, leaf bundles, taxonomies and terms. The slash-count index mapping is somewhat fragile, slugs are not applied to `:sections` permalink expansions, and the integration test covers the main scenarios well.

This fixes the reported root-module case: import blocks are tracked by owning module, so every same-module block for a for_each resource is kept, and declaration order plus the cloned path are good touches. However, any parent-module import still silently drops all of a child module's imports for that resource, even for different instances (its own fixture asserts this). That is the same silent-drop failure in a cross-module form, and together with the changed return type it likely explains why only 1 of 3 hidden tests passed.

Correctly fixes the same-module case: all import blocks are now kept in a slice instead of being deduplicated by ConfigResource, and it also fixes an append aliasing bug on cfg.Path. However, a parent-module import still drops every child-module import for that resource, even ones targeting other instances (its own fixture drops child b["x"] when the root imports b["z"]), so the silent-drop behaviour remains across modules. It also changes the public return type, which likely explains failing 2 of 3 hidden tests; the added unit and plan tests are solid.

Fixes the round-trip loss by wrapping a parenthesised `*NumberLiteral` in a unary-ADD `*DurationExpr` with `Wrapped` set, and keeps the positive-duration and division/modulo-by-zero checks working through the new `constDurationValue` helper; tests cover printer round-trips, parse errors and promqltest evaluation, though the synthetic unary-plus node is a slightly indirect representation, its position ranges exclude the parens, and it moves plain wrapped literals from `OriginalOffset` to `OriginalOffsetExpr`.

Wrapping a bare NumberLiteral in a Wrapped unary-ADD DurationExpr fixes the lost parentheses at the root, and the new constDurationValue helper keeps zero/negative-duration and division/modulo-by-zero validation working through the new wrapper. Tests cover printer round-trips, parser error cases and evaluation; the only cost is that `(N)` now yields OriginalOffsetExpr/RangeExpr instead of a folded constant, matching how other duration expressions already behave.

The patch adds `--once` to the shared option flags, rejects conflicting CLI shortcut flags, and rewrites the consolidated config into a 1-VU/1-iteration shared-iterations scenario that keeps exec, env, tags and options, so it works across run, cloud run and archive. It has thorough unit and integration tests; one minor gap is that if K6_ITERATIONS-style env vars make consolidation drop the script's scenario, the scenario is silently lost instead of raising an error.

Applies the --once transform after consolidation, keeps exec/env/tags/options for a single scenario, rejects multiple scenarios and the conflicting shortcut flags with InvalidConfig, and is backed by thorough unit and integration tests (run, archive, cloud upload, env-var overrides); minor oddities include `null.NewInt(1, false)` for VUs and a package-level slice for the conflicting flags.

The design is sound: a ReturnError sentinel is panicked out of evalCall, recovered per template in walkTemplate and executeWithState, unwrapped in doInclude, re-panicked past try, and the old AST rewrite and HasReturn are removed. However, it fails one hidden test and the package suite, and it rewrites an existing test's expected error message to fit the new behavior. It also leaves a dangling 'Store away the return node' comment and changes how `{{ return x | f }}` is evaluated compared with the old behavior.

The patch implements the sentinel-error approach the issue proposed and removes the old partial-wrapper transformation; one hidden PR test and the package suite still fail, so some semantics probably differ from what is expected. The approach: a ReturnError is panicked from evalCall, recovered per `{{ template }}` and in executeWithState, and swallowed by ExecuteWithContext. It uses the fork-script rename mechanism correctly and keeps `return add . 42` working through argument wrapping. Minor issues are a dangling comment for a removed field and a rewritten existing test expectation.
